summary.one_liner: OpenChronicle is an open-source, local-first memory layer that captures macOS accessibility-tree context and turns it into Markdown and SQLite memory that any tool-capable LLM agent can query.
keywords: give ai assistant memory of my work
summary.what_it_does: OpenChronicle runs on macOS and watches accessibility events from the active apps. It parses focused elements, visible text and URLs into a capture buffer, then normalizes them into timeline blocks. A session manager groups activity into sessions using idle and app-switch rules, and a reducer and classifier turn those sessions into Markdown files such as user-, project-, tool-, topic-, person-, org- and daily event- notes. The Markdown is indexed in local SQLite with FTS5. The daemon exposes an MCP endpoint so agents can query this memory through tools. The README says the model can be local or cloud, via Ollama, LM Studio, OpenAI, Anthropic or any LiteLLM-compatible provider.
use_cases: give a coding agent memory of what I was working on
recall past decisions and context across sessions
track which tools, projects and people I work with
query my recent screen activity from an AI assistant
keep private AI memory on my own Mac
build custom memory parsers for apps like browsers or editors
notable: AX-tree-first capture, with screenshots planned as a secondary signal, to keep memory compact and cheap to process
Memory stored as human-readable Markdown on disk plus a local SQLite index
Session-aware writing that groups activity into sessions instead of per-snapshot logs
Model-agnostic: local or cloud LLM providers, with MCP as the best-supported agent interface today
caveats: macOS only (requires macOS 13+ and Xcode Command Line Tools), and the README calls it early alpha at v0.1.0
MCP is the best-supported integration path today; other agent integrations are described more loosely
The MCP endpoint URL is blank in the README, so the exact address must be found in docs/mcp.md
